codecademy

in case you eventually don't like online courses, I will tell you how I learned:

website design

perhaps you will be interested in the front-end side first, so, HTML, then CSS, then Javascript. Then the backend stuff later.

know some very basic HTML

Good start. Now learn CSS then. But not just the basic. Make sure you understand CSS box model very well. Then learn responsive design concept.

The next step is to revisit HTML. This time, learn how to use HTML5 new tags and semantics. It shouldn't be hard if you know the basic. When learning "HTML5", you will find javascript codes. Avoid that for now.

Now, create a responsive web page with pure CSS and HTML. This one will be harder than you may thought.

Then do it again with a CSS framework like Bootstrap. Again, skip the javascript parts for now.

Done? Do another one. And another one. It becomes easier and easier and it should be beautiful.

Your are a confident web designer now. It will feel awesome. But you're not a front-end web developer yet :p.

NOW FOR THE TOUGH PART. Read a beginner book on Javascript (for example Eloquent Javascript). For HTML and CSS, you can learn it fairly well enough without a book, but I really recommend to read books on programming (HTML and CSS is just structures, not real programming).

After you read the beginner book, learn jQuery. At this point you will figure out your own way of learning. People will say jQuery is shit and bloat and other things, but the truth is 80% of websites use jQuery. It's a valuable skill. After you have the idea how that thing works, play with jQuery plugins and bootstrap plugins.

Now talk to your friend which is a programmer. Ask them what is database, how stuff works in the back end, what kind of things that a programmer should now in the back end. After you get the basic idea and know some terms, read about them again on the internet.

Congratulation, you can get a job as junior front end developer now.

Learn the syntax and how to make it works for the sake of database course only, because later you will be doing more back-end stuff in javascript, because you already know it better and it seems have a very bright future.

After understanding databases, you know exactly what the back end developers are doing. You will be excited to build a complete website. Well, do that! But here's the key to make it not a pain in the ass: learn a framework. And because I've already recommended javascript for the backend, I recommend this javascript (node.js) framework: sails.js. At this point, you may also want to read another book like Javascript: The Good Parts.. I also recommend you to use postgresql instead of mongodb that's popular in node.js world. A bit about my experience in learning back end: I actually went with CodeIgniter (PHP) and mysql. It gets the job done too, but many people leave it for newer technology. Hey guys. I've recently gotten a job and I've got an office mate(we share a room) who smokes(not inside the office, but it carries in on his clothes). It's on an internal part of the building, so plants would not receive a lot of sunlight. Do you guys have a recommendation for an air purifier that would filter out the smoke? I'd rather not simply just mask the smoke.
Need help buying an air purifier

There are actually quite a few options you could try.

  1. Baking soda: it will remove most any foul smell from the air. Great for controlling trash odors as well.

  2. Activated charcoal: Actually used in a wide variety of household utilities; activated charcoal will help to remove odors.

  3. Air purifier: Self explanatory.

  4. Air Ionizer: Essentially produces negative ions that will bond with the organic particles, make them heavy, and cause them to fall to the ground.

All pretty good options. I personally would go for one of the silent options if it's not too bad, but if it's quite noticeable maybe getting one of the electric ones might motivate him to at least face down wind to decrease the amount of smoke that hits his clothes.

I purchased this unit when it was on sale at meh.com http://www.amazon.com/dp/B00HZDVK7M/?tag=buyitbutton-20

It's cheaper than an air ionizer, and it has a washable filter for dirt. You can add in an activated charcoal filter for smells.

Ionizers generate ozone, which causes breathing problems. Consumer Reports found that several models generated unhealthy amounts of ozone.

Air purifiers filter air mechanically- your choice of filter which fits in the purifier is critical. You will need a HEPA filter to remove any smoke. NOT a HEPA-type filter as many are advertised.

Reusable HEPA filters do not exist. You will need replaceable filters.

For reducing smoke smell you will need activated carbon, too.

Unfortunately I do not have any specific recommendations. If you see some, watch out for affiliate tags- people may be trying to sell you something to make money off you. I do not recommend following links with these tags.
